groups.ask: What are go, grow and glow foods?

explain.say: Your body is a bit like a car. It needs fuel to go, parts to grow, and care to keep it shiny. Foods can do all three jobs! Look at the board. Let's sort your favourite foods into go, grow and glow.

items.label: Grow foods
items.ask: What should be on a healthy plate?

faq.q: What are go, grow and glow foods?
faq.a: Go foods, like rice and bread, give energy. Grow foods, like beans, eggs and fish, build the body. Glow foods, fruit and vegetables, keep you healthy with vitamins and minerals.
Protein is the building material of your body. It helps muscles, skin and hair grow and helps repair cuts and bruises. Beans, lentils, eggs, fish, meat and milk are rich in it.

faq.q: What should be on a healthy plate?
faq.a: A good guide is half the plate fruit and vegetables, a quarter energy foods like rice or bread, and a quarter protein foods like beans, eggs or fish, with water to drink.
Sweets are fine as a small treat now and then, but they have lots of sugar and few vitamins, and too much sugar is bad for teeth and health.
asks: Can I eat sweets every day?

faq.q: Why do we need fruit and vegetables?
faq.a: Fruit and vegetables give vitamins, minerals and fibre. They help you fight germs, keep your eyes and skin healthy, and keep your tummy working well.

facts: Healthy-eating guides such as the Harvard Healthy Eating Plate suggest filling about half the plate with vegetables and fruit.
Proteins supply the building blocks the body uses to grow and repair tissues.
